# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Tune WebACL `response-id-on-page` so the AWS-managed SQLi rule group stops false-positive blocking legitimate natural-language searches on `/search`, while preserving SQL-injection protection everywhere else. Two surgical edits: (1) override sub-rule `SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS` in `AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet` (Priority 300) from Block to Count; (2) add a new higher-priority rule `block-sqli-queryargs-except-search` (Priority 302) that re-blocks on the label `awswaf:managed:aws:sql-database:SQLi_QueryArguments` for any URI not starting with `/search`.

## Reasoning
Benign searches like `credit UNION members SELECT best savings plan` were blocked because `/search` forwards raw user text as the `q` query argument, and `SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS` flags UNION/SELECT keyword co-occurrence at LOW sensitivity even in natural language. A label-match exception scoped to `/search` is the narrowest fix: a full scope-down would disable ALL SQLi sub-rules on `/search`; a plain Count override would weaken query-arg SQLi protection site-wide. This keeps `SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS` blocking on every path except `/search` and all other SQLi sub-rules blocking everywhere. Affected: WebACL `response-id-on-page`, [redacted ARN], account 012345678901_1, us-east-1.
